metadata.title: ETSI TS 103 701 V2.1.1 (2025-05): Cyber Security for Consumer Internet of Things: Conformance Assessment of Baseline Requirements (test cases)
metadata.remarks:
The test cases of clause 5 of ETSI TS 103 701 V2.1.1, the conformance assessment of the provisions of ETSI EN 303 645 / ETSI TS 103 645, one control per test case, in the structure of the TS: TSO (group) -> test group (group: its objective, and the provisions it addresses in props "provision") -> test case (control). The statement of a control is the test purpose; its parts are the test units (one item each, with their notes and examples) and the assignment of verdict; its assessment method is EXAMINE for a conceptual test case and TEST for a functional one.

Made from the text of the PDF by a script; to be checked against the PDF before use in an assessment. Not included: clauses 1 to 4 and the annexes (the ICS and IXIT pro formas, the mapping, the examples).

parts.name: objective
parts.prose: The test group addresses the provision 5.0-1.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the justifications for recommendations that are considered to be not applicable for or not …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the justifications for recommendations that are considered to be not applicable for or not fulfilled by the DUT.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall check whether a justification is given in the ICS for each recommendation that is considered to be not applicable for or not fulfilled by the DUT.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- a justification is given for every recommendation that is considered to be not applicable for the DUT; and
- a justification is given for every recommendation that is considered to be not fulfilled by the DUT.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.1-1.

This test group addresses all states of the DUT with the exception of factory default.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the password-based authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT or for …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the password-based authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall assess for all password-based authentication mechanisms in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that are used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description" and where passwords are not defined by the user according to "Authentication Factor" and used in any state other than the factory default whether the "Password Generation Mechanism" ensures that passwords are unique per device.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- each password of a password-based authentication mechanism used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication in any state other than the factory default, that is not defined by the user, is unique per device.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment of the password-based authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT or for …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment of the password-based authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication concerning the completeness of the IXIT documentation a), the passwords defined by the user b) and the generation mechanisms c).

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall functionally assess whether password-based authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication that are not documented in IXIT 1-AuthMech are available via a network interface on the DUT or described in the user manual.

EXAMPLE: Network scanning tools allow for discovery of network-based authentication mechanisms.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each password-based authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech that is used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description", the TL shall functionally check whether the user is required to define all passwords that are user-defined according to "Authentication Factor" before being used.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall functionally assess whether all passwords of the DUT, that are not defined by the user according to "Authentication Factor" in IXIT 1-AuthMech and used in any state other than the factory default, do not violate the description of the "Password Generation Mechanism".

NOTE: The assessment of the quality of the generation mechanism is part of test group 5.1-2.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- every discovered password-based authentication mechanism used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication is documented in the IXIT; and
- the user is required to define all passwords before being used, that are stated as defined by the user in the IXIT; and
- there is no indication that the generation of a not user-defined password of the DUT used in any state other than the factory default differs from the generation mechanism described in the IXIT.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose: The test group addresses the provision 5.1-2.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the generation mechanisms of pre-installed passwords

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the generation mechanisms of pre-installed passwords.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess for each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that is used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description" and where pre-installed passwords are used according to "Authentication Factor", whether the generation mechanism in "Password Generation Mechanism" induces obvious regularities in the resulting passwords.

NOTE 1: Incremental counters (such as "password1", "password2" and so on) can be obvious regularities.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess whether the generation mechanism induces common strings or other common patterns in the resulting passwords.

NOTE 2: Common strings can be those contained in password dictionaries, such as for example: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/static-assets/documents/PwnedPasswordsTop100k.txt.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess whether the generation mechanism induces passwords, that are related in an obvious way to public information.

NOTE 3: Public information can be MAC addresses, Wi-Fi® SSIDs, name, type and description of the device.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess whether the generation mechanism induces passwords, that are considered appropriate in terms of complexity.

NOTE 4: In this context complexity is linked to the probability of guessing the password while applying the information an attacker has. The length of a password is one important aspect to consider for a password's complexity.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- no obvious regularities in pre-installed passwords are found; and
- no common strings or other common patterns in pre-installed passwords are found; and
- the generation mechanisms for pre-installed passwords do not induce passwords, that are related in an obvious way to public information; and
- the generation mechanisms for pre-installed passwords are considered appropriate in terms of complexity.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment of the generation mechanisms of pre-installed passwords

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment of the generation mechanisms of pre-installed passwords.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that is used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description" and where pre-installed passwords are used according to "Authentication Factor", the TL shall functionally assess whether the generation mechanism is plausibly implemented in accordance to the description in "Password Generation Mechanism".

EXAMPLE: The description of the "Password Generation Mechanism" states, that passwords consist of 8 digits containing at least one character of each group uppercase letters, lowercase letters and numbers. The verification that the corresponding passwords of the DUT match the given length of 8 digits, containing at least one character of the stated groups and do not contain special characters can be helpful to collect an indication.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- for each pre-installed password there is no indication, that its generation differs from the generation mechanism described in the IXIT.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose: The test group addresses the provision 5.1-2A.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment whether passwords are used for machine-to-machine authentication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment whether passwords are used for machine-to-machine authentication.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess for each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that is used for machine-to- machine authentication according to "Description", whether the type of attribute used for authentication in "Authentication Factor" includes passwords.

NOTE: Pre shared keys that follow best practice can be appropriate depending on the operating environment, risk and usage.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- no authentication mechanism used for machine-to-machine authentication uses passwords.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment whether passwords are used for machine-to-machine authentication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment whether passwords are used for machine-to-machine authentication.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall apply test unit a) as specified in the Test case 5.1-1-2 to every referenced "Authentication Mechanism" in IXIT 1-AuthMech.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech used for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description", the TL shall functionally assess whether the authentication process accepts passwords.

EXAMPLE 1: Using man in the middle methods to break encryption and get access to the machine-to-machine authentication API.

EXAMPLE 2: Try to change operation mode of the machine-to-machine authentication mechanism to accept passwords or weak Pre-Shared Key.

NOTE: Hardcoding passwords in Machine-to-Machine (M2M) communication poses a significant security risk, as they can be easily exposed if files are compromised or shared. A more secure approach would involve using token-based authentication (e.g. API keys, OAuth2) or certificate-based methods like mutual TLS (mTLS), which are designed for secure automated system interactions. The TL may check whether for example such mechanisms are used.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- for all authentication mechanisms used for machine-to-machine authentication there is no indication that passwords are accepted.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.1-3.

According to ETSI TS 103 645 [1]/ETSI EN 303 645 [2] best practice cryptography is defined as cryptography that is suitable for the corresponding use case and has no indication of a feasible attack with current readily available techniques. In the present test group, the term "use case" considers the properties of technology, operating environment, risk and usage context.

The objective of this test group is to assess, firstly, whether the cryptographic methods provide the security guarantees that are necessary for the authentication mechanisms and, secondly, whether the cryptographic methods are not known to be vulnerable to a feasible attack.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the cryptography used for the authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the cryptography used for the authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication concerning the use of best practice cryptography (a-c) and the vulnerability to a feasible attack d).

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that is used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description", the TL shall assess whether the "Security Guarantees" are appropriate for the use case, at least integrity and authenticity are required to be fulfilled.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that is used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description", the TL shall assess whether the mechanism according to "Description" is appropriate to achieve the "Security Guarantees".

NOTE 1: A holistic approach is required to assess the security of the mechanism.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that is used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description", the TL shall assess whether the "Cryptographic Details" are considered as best practice for the use case based on a reference catalogue. If "Cryptographic Details" are not included in a reference catalogue for the corresponding use case (e.g. novel cryptography), the SO shall provide evidence, e.g. a risk analysis, to justify the cryptography is appropriate as best practice for the use case. In such case the TL shall assess whether the evidence is appropriate and reliable for the use case.

NOTE 2: A list of use case based examples for best practice cryptography is given in ETSI TR 103 621 [i.7]. Moreover, general reference catalogues of best practice cryptography are available, for example:

 SOGIS Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms (https://www.sogis.eu).

NOTE 3: A cryptographic algorithm or primitive that is deprecated with regard to its desired security property (e.g. SHA1 for collision resistance) or that relies on a cryptographic parameter (e.g. key-size) that is not appropriate, taking into account the intended lifetime of the DUT and crypto agility, cannot be considered as best practice cryptography.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that is used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description", the TL shall assess whether the "Cryptographic Details" are not known to be vulnerable to a feasible attack for the desired security property on the base of the "Security Guarantees" by reference to competent cryptanalytic reports.

NOTE 4: Competent cryptanalytic reports are typically published in the scientific literature or, alternatively, are to be provided by the SO. Further, clause D.2 provides information about the expected attack potential for level basic.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if for all authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication:

- the security guarantees are appropriate for the use case; and
- the mechanism is appropriate to achieve the security guarantees with respect to the use case; and
- all used cryptographic details are considered as best practice for the use case; and
- all used cryptographic details are not known to be vulnerable to a feasible attack for the desired security property.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment of the cryptography used for authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment of the cryptography used for authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, that is used to authenticate users against the DUT or for machine-to-machine authentication according to "Description", the TL shall functionally assess whether the described "Cryptographic Details" are used by the DUT.

EXAMPLE 1: Using a protocol analyser or packet sniffer tool for network-based mechanisms.

EXAMPLE 2: If a PKI certificate based authentication is used, sniffing the used certificates and comparing the properties with the described cryptography in the IXIT can be helpful to collect an indication.

EXAMPLE 3: If the underlying communication protocol of the authentication mechanism enables different security modes for the communication, trying to downgrade the security mode can be helpful to collect an indication.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- there is no indication that any used cryptographic setting differs from its IXIT documentation.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose: The test group addresses the provision 5.1-4.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of whether authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT provide simple …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of whether authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT provide simple mechanisms to change authentication values.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For every authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech where "Description" indicates that the mechanism is used for user authentication, the TL shall assess whether the values of authentication factors can be changed by a user or administrator according to the "Authentication factor".

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For every authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech where "Description" indicates that the mechanism is used for user authentication, the TL shall assess whether the information provided to the user or administrator considers the mechanism and describes how to change authentication values for the mechanism in a manner that is understandable for a user with limited technical knowledge (see clause D.3) according to "Documentation of Change Mechanisms" in IXIT 2-UserInfo.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- for all authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT the values of authentication factors can be changed by a user or administrator; and
- for all authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT information is provided to the user which describes how to change the values of authentication factors in a manner that is understandable for a user with limited technical knowledge.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment whether authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT provide simple …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment whether authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT provide simple mechanisms to change authentication values.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall perform a change of the authentication values for all user authentication mechanisms in IXIT 1-AuthMech as documented in "Documentation of Change Mechanisms" in IXIT 2-UserInfo.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall functionally assess whether all changes of user authentication values are successful.

EXAMPLE: The old authentication value is no longer valid and the new authentication value is valid after a change.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- all mechanisms for the user to change authentication values for authentication mechanisms used to authenticate users against the DUT work as described.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose: The test group addresses the provision 5.1-5.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the mechanisms to make successful brute force attacks via network interfaces impracticable

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the mechanisms to make successful brute force attacks via network interfaces impracticable.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess whether for each authentication mechanism in IXIT 1-AuthMech, where "Description" indicates that the mechanism is directly addressable via a network interface, the mechanism in "Brute Force Prevention" makes successful brute force attacks via network interfaces impracticable.

NOTE 1: Methods to mitigate brute force attacks are, among others:

 Time delays between consecutive failed attempts to authenticate.

 A limited number of authentication attempts, followed by a suspension period where no login is allowed.

 A limited number of authentication attempts, followed by locking the authentication mechanism.

 Appropriate entropy for authentication values based on best practice cryptography.

 Two-factor authentication.

NOTE 2: There are best practices for brute force protection available, e.g. https://owasp.org/www- community/controls/Blocking_Brute_Force_Attacks.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- the documented mechanisms make successful brute force attacks via network interfaces impracticable.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment of the mechanisms to make successful brute force attacks via network interfaces impracticable …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment of the mechanisms to make successful brute force attacks via network interfaces impracticable concerning the completeness of the IXIT documentation a) and the corresponding mechanisms b).

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall functionally assess whether there exist further network-based authentication mechanisms, that are not listed in IXIT 1-AuthMech.

NOTE: Methods for functionally checking for network-based authentication methods include network scanners such as "nmap", or wireless sniffers such as a BLE dongle.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall attempt to brute force every network-based authentication mechanism described in IXIT 1-AuthMech.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- ever discovered network-based authentication mechanism is documented in the IXIT; and
- for all authentication mechanism via network interfaces there is no indication that the implementation of brute force prevention differs from its IXIT documentation.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

groups.title: Implement a means to manage reports of vulnerabilities

parts.name: objective
parts.prose: The test group addresses the provision 5.2-1.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the publication of the vulnerability disclosure policy

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the publication of the vulnerability disclosure policy.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess whether access to the publication as described in "Publication of Vulnerability Disclosure Policy" in IXIT 2-UserInfo is possible without meeting criteria such as user account, i.e. whether anybody can access the documentation.

NOTE: A website of the manufacturer is considered as appropriate.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- the publication of the vulnerability disclosure policy is available for anybody.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment of the publication of the vulnerability disclosure policy

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment of the publication of the vulnerability disclosure policy.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall functionally check whether the vulnerability disclosure policy is publicly accessible as described in "Publication of Vulnerability Disclosure Policy" in IXIT 2-UserInfo.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall functionally check whether the policy contains:

- contact information; and
- timelines for initial acknowledgement of receipt of a vulnerability report; and
- timelines for when the person who reported the issue will receive status updates until the resolution of the reported issues.

NOTE: Different notations are possible to describe time values in the timetable (e.g. "7 days", "quickly", etc.). ETSI TR 103 838 [i.11] contains an example for a vulnerability disclosure policy including timelines for initial acknowledgement of receipt and a proposal for information on timelines for status updates until the resolution of the reported issues. The time needed to find a solution can vary depending e.g. on the criticality of the disclosed vulnerability.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- the vulnerability disclosure policy is publicly accessible; and
- the vulnerability disclosure policy contains contact information and timelines for initial acknowledgement of receipt of a vulnerability report and timelines for when the person who reported the issue will receive status updates until the resolution of the reported issues.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose: The test group addresses the provision 5.2-2.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the manner in which vulnerabilities are acted on a) and the confirmation that the …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the manner in which vulnerabilities are acted on a) and the confirmation that the preconditions for the implementation are ensured b).

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess whether the "Action" and the "Time Frame" of each disclosed vulnerability in IXIT 3-VulnTypes facilitate that vulnerabilities are acted on in a timely manner under consideration of the vulnerability disclosure policy according to "Publication of Vulnerability Disclosure Policy" in IXIT 2-UserInfo.

NOTE 1: The consideration of severity and criticality of the addressed vulnerabilities and the kind of vulnerability (e.g. firmware, hardware or software) is helpful.

NOTE 2: The amount of collaboration between the involved entities, the number of process steps and clearly defined responsibilities are important indicators for a timely deployment.

NOTE 3: In the case that a third party is involved (e.g. a software library vendor) the documentation of the point of contacts and defined procedures for the collaboration are indicators for a timely deployment.

NOTE 4: The comparison with the time frame for acting on vulnerabilities of similar types of IoT products is helpful.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall check whether "Confirmation of Vulnerability Actions" in IXIT 4-Conf states a confirmation.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- there is no indication that any described kind of vulnerability is not acted on timely; and
- a confirmation for the implementation is given.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of continuous monitoring, identifying and rectifying security vulnerabilities concerning the …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of continuous monitoring, identifying and rectifying security vulnerabilities concerning the described procedures (a-c) and the confirmation that the preconditions for the implementation are ensured d).

parts.name: item

parts.name: item

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall check whether "Confirmation of Vulnerability Monitoring" in IXIT 4-Conf states a confirmation.

The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- the described way is suited for continuously monitoring for security vulnerabilities; and
- the described way is suited for identifying security vulnerabilities; and
- the described way is suited for rectifying security vulnerabilities; and
- a confirmation for the implementation is given.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-1.

This test group handles the updatability of each software component that is not immutable due to a security reason. According to ETSI TS 103 645 [1]/ETSI EN 303 645 [2] "securely updateable" means that there are adequate measures to prevent an attacker misusing the update mechanism.

NOTE: Any discovery of software components in the DUT is out of scope of this test group.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the updatability of software components concerning the absence of software updates a) and the …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the updatability of software components concerning the absence of software updates a) and the update mechanisms b).

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each software component in IXIT 6-SoftComp with an empty list in "Update Mechanism", the TL shall assess whether the software component is immutable due to security reasons as described in the justification for the absence of software updates.

EXAMPLE 1: An IoT device can contain separate microcontrollers from the main system which are only internally addressable. Those microcontrollers typically act as an internal service provider (e.g. temperature controller of a smart wine rack) sometimes without update functionality. A software update for those components can be beyond practicability for the DUT.

EXAMPLE 2: For some implementations, the security concept for the DUT can require that a component is not changeable (e.g. software which is part of the trust chain of the bootloader). Therefore, the component is not updateable for superordinate security reasons.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall apply all test units as specified in the Test case 5.3-2-1 to every referenced "Update Mechanism" in IXIT 6-SoftComp.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- for all software components without the ability for software updates, a software update is not possible for practicability reasons or security reasons; and
- no update mechanism can be misused by an attacker.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:

This test group examines that at least one update mechanism for the secure installation of software updates exists.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the update installation mechanism concerning adequate measures to prevent an attacker misusing …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the update installation mechanism concerning adequate measures to prevent an attacker misusing the update installation on the DUT.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the design of the update mechanism prevents misuse from an attacker according to the "Security Guarantees", the corresponding "Description", "Cryptographic Details" and "Initiation and Interaction".

NOTE: The consideration of the baseline attacker model described in clause D.2 is helpful for the examination.

EXAMPLE: A misuse can be the installation of an old software update to downgrade the security capabilities of the DUT or the injection of malware by manipulating a valid update.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- one update mechanism of the DUT cannot be misused by an attacker.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment of the effectiveness of the update mechanism to avoid misuse

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment of the effectiveness of the update mechanism to avoid misuse.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall devise functional attacks to misuse the update mechanism based on the "Description".

EXAMPLE 1: If applicable try a Man-In-The-Middle attack (MITM) between the DUT and the update server.

NOTE 1: An attack can be trying to resume the sequence of update steps after some failure of a specific update step, installing an older firmware version that contains security vulnerabilities, or changing one byte in a signed firmware to check that it is rejected.

NOTE 2: There are multiple ways to perform an indication based security analysis even if no update is available during the assessment, e.g. verify a file based update mechanism on the base of old update packages.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall attempt to misuse each update mechanism on the base of the devised adverse actions and assess whether the design of the mechanism (see "Description", the "Cryptographic Details" and "Initiation and Interaction") effectively prevents the misuse of software updates as described in the "Security Guarantees".

EXAMPLE 2: If a file based update mechanism uses signature verifications, providing a manipulated update package to the DUT can be helpful to collect indications.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- there is no indication that a misuse of one update mechanism of the DUT is possible.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-3.

According to ETSI TS 103 645 [1]/ETSI EN 303 645 [2] in terms of this test group an update that is simple to apply will be automatically applied, or initiated using an associated service (such as a mobile application) or via a web interface on the device. However, this does not exclude alternative solutions.

The focus of the provision is on triggering the update from the user perspective and verifying whether the user is provided with the ability to update all software components in a simple manner. This case is given if each software component is updatable with at least one simple update mechanism.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the update mechanisms concerning simplicity for the user to apply an update

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the update mechanisms concerning simplicity for the user to apply an update.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each software component in IXIT 6-SoftComp, the TL shall assess whether at least one "Update Mechanism" is described, which is simple for the user to apply according to "Initiation and Interaction" in IXIT 7-UpdMech based on the following factors:

- the software update is automatically applied without requiring any user interaction; or
- the software update is initiated via an associated service; or
- the software update is initiated via a web interface on the device; or
- the software update uses a comparable approach which is applicable for the user with limited technical knowledge (see clause D.3).

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- each software component is covered by at least one update mechanism, which is simple for the user to apply.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: objective

controls.title: Conceptual assessment whether a secure update mechanism is enabled during the initialization of the DUT

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment whether a secure update mechanism is enabled during the initialization of the DUT.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall identify all automatic update mechanisms in IXIT 7-UpdMech by assessing whether the mechanism allows the performance of updates without requiring any user interaction according to "Initiation and Interaction".

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each automatic update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech the TL shall check whether the user's consent to enable the mechanism queried during initialization, is described in IXIT 26-UserDec.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each automatic update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, where the user's consent to enable the mechanism is queried and granted according to "Configuration" during initialization, the TL shall check whether the automatic mechanism can be enabled by the DUT.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- at least one user's consent to enable an automatic update mechanism is queried during initialization; and
- each automatic update mechanism for which the user's consent to enable the mechanism is queried and granted during initialization is enabled by the DUT.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment whether automatic secure update mechanisms are enabled during the initialization of the DUT after …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment whether automatic secure update mechanisms are enabled during the initialization of the DUT after user's consent.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: during the initialization process of the DUT, the TL shall check whether the user's consent to enable an automatic secure update mechanism is queried; and

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
for each automatic secure update mechanism for which the user's consent to enable the mechanisms is queried and granted during the initialization of the DUT, the TL shall check whether the mechanism is enabled after the initialization of the DUT; and

NOTE: The TL may try to simulate the availability of a new update to trigger the automatic secure update mechanism. In the case of time-based mechanisms, for instance the TL may try to modify the time of the device.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: for each automatic secure update mechanism for which the user's consent to enable the mechanisms is queried and denied during the initialization of the DUT, the TL shall check whether the mechanism is disabled after the initialization of the DUT.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- the user's consent to enable at least one automatic secure update mechanisms is queried during the initialization of the DUT; and
- for each automatic secure update mechanism where user's consent to enable the mechanism is queried and granted during the initialization of the DUT, the update mechanisms is enabled; and
- for each automatic secure update mechanism where user's consent to enable the mechanism is queried and denied during the initialization of the DUT, the update mechanisms is disabled.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-5.

The focus of the provision is on the ability to check for security updates for the software of the DUT. This case is given if each software component is updatable with at least one update mechanism checking for security updates after initialization.

NOTE: The check can also be performed by an associated service of the DUT.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the update mechanisms concerning the checks for available security updates

parts.name: statement

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if every software component is covered by at least one update mechanism, where:

- at least one secure update mechanism checks for the availability of security updates after or during initialization of the DUT.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-6A.

NOTE: The entry "Initiation and Interaction" in IXIT 7-UpdMech indicates whether it is an automatic update mechanism in combination with the test units in Test group 5.3-4A.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the configuration of automatic updates

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the configuration of automatic updates.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall identify all automatic update mechanisms in IXIT 7-UpdMech by assessing whether the mechanism supports updates without requiring any user interaction according to "Initiation and Interaction".

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech that provides automatic software updates, the TL shall check whether it provides the user with the ability to:

- enable; and
- disable; and
- postpone

the automatic installation of updates according to "Configuration" in IXIT 7-UpdMech.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- for all automatic update mechanisms, the user is provided with the ability to enable, disable or postpone automatic installation of updates.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the functional assessment of the configuration of automatic updates.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:

- disable; and
- postpone

automatic installation of updates in the configuration of the DUT.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-7.

According to ETSI TS 103 645 [1]/ETSI EN 303 645 [2] best practice cryptography is defined as cryptography that is suitable for the corresponding use case and has no indication of a feasible attack with current readily available techniques. In the present test group, the term "use case" considers the properties of technology, operating environment, risk and usage context.

The objective of this test group is to assess, firstly, whether the cryptographic methods provide the security guarantees that are necessary for the secure update mechanisms and, secondly, whether the cryptographic methods are not known to be vulnerable to a feasible attack.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the cryptography used for the update mechanisms concerning the use of best practice …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the cryptography used for the update mechanisms concerning the use of best practice cryptography (a-c) and the vulnerability to a feasible attack d).

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the "Security Guarantees" are appropriate for the use case of secure updates, at least the protection of integrity and authenticity are required to be fulfilled.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the mechanism according to "Description" is appropriate to achieve the "Security Guarantees".

NOTE 1: A holistic approach is required to assess the security of the mechanism.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the "Cryptographic Details" are considered as best practice for the use case of secure updates based on a reference catalogue. If "Cryptographic Details" are not included in a reference catalogue for the corresponding use case (e.g. novel cryptography), the SO shall provide evidences, e.g. a risk analysis, to justify the cryptography is appropriate as best practice for the use case. In such case the TL shall assess whether the evidence is appropriate and reliable for the use case.

NOTE 2: A list of use case based examples for best practice cryptography is given in ETSI TR 103 621 [i.7]. Moreover, general reference catalogues of best practice cryptography are available, for example:

 SOGIS Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms (https://www.sogis.eu).

NOTE 3: A cryptographic algorithm or primitive that is deprecated with regard to its desired security property (e.g. SHA1 for collision resistance) or that relies on a cryptographic parameter (e.g. key-size) that is not appropriate, taking into account the intended lifetime of the DUT and crypto agility, cannot be considered as best practice cryptography.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the "Cryptographic Details" are not known to be vulnerable to a feasible attack for the desired security property on the base of the "Security Guarantees" by reference to competent cryptanalytic reports.

NOTE 4: Competent cryptanalytic reports are typically published in the scientific literature or, alternatively, are to be provided by the SO. Further, clause D.2 provides information about the expected attack potential for level basic.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if for all update mechanisms:

- the security guarantees are appropriate for the use case of secure updates; and
- the mechanism is appropriate to achieve the security guarantees with respect to the use case; and
- all used cryptographic details are considered as best practice for the use case; and
- all used cryptographic details are not known to be vulnerable to a feasible attack for the desired security property.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-8.

The assessment focuses on the management procedures that are necessary for deploying security updates timely.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the manner in which security updates are deployed a) and the confirmation that the …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the manner in which security updates are deployed a) and the confirmation that the preconditions for the implementation are ensured b).

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess whether the "Description" and the "Time Frame" of each security update procedure in IXIT 8-UpdProc facilitate that security updates are deployed in a timely manner.

NOTE 1: The consideration of severity and criticality of the addressed security vulnerabilities and the kind of vulnerability (e.g. firmware, hardware or software) is helpful.

NOTE 2: The amount of collaboration between the involved entities, the number of process steps and clearly defined responsibilities are important indicators for a timely deployment.

NOTE 3: In the case that a third party is involved (e.g. a software library vendor) the documentation of the point of contacts and defined procedures for the collaboration are indicators for a timely deployment.

NOTE 4: The comparison with the time frame for security updates of similar types of IoT products is helpful.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall check whether "Confirmation of Update Procedures" in IXIT 4-Conf states a confirmation.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- there is an indication that the described management procedure allows a timely deployment of security updates; and
- a confirmation for the implementation is given.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-9.

Verification of authenticity means the demonstration that the software update is not forged, including, in particular, the authenticity of the software update in regard to its source (manufacturer) and target (DUT).

Verification of integrity means the demonstration that the software update is not tampered.

The assessment focuses on the verification of authenticity and integrity that is performed by the DUT itself prior to the installation of the software update.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the verification of software updates concerning authenticity a), integrity b) and the …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the verification of software updates concerning authenticity a), integrity b) and the performing entity (c-d).

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the authenticity of software updates in regard to its source (manufacturer) and target (DUT) is suitably verified according to "Security Guarantees" and the corresponding "Cryptographic Details".

NOTE 1: There are different ways of verifying the authenticity of a software update in regard to its source and target.

NOTE 2: The validation of authenticity by the DUT serves primary for the rejection of untrustworthy software updates.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the integrity of software updates is suitably verified according to "Security Guarantees" and the corresponding "Cryptographic Details".

NOTE 3: The validation of integrity by the DUT serves primary for the detection injected malicious code in a valid software update.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall check whether the authenticity verification is performed by the DUT itself according to "Security Guarantees".

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall check whether the integrity verification is performed by the DUT itself according to "Security Guarantees".

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- each update mechanism is effective for the verification of authenticity of software updates; and
- each update mechanism is effective for the verification of integrity of software updates; and
- the verification of authenticity and integrity of software updates is performed by the DUT itself.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-10.

NOTE: The entry "Description" in IXIT 7-UpdMech indicates whether it is a network based update mechanism.

The validation of the trust relationship is essential to ensure that a non-authorized entity (e.g. device management platform or device) cannot install malicious code.

The essential difference between this test group and Test group 5.3-9 is that the verification of authenticity and integrity has to be performed via a trust relationship, i.e. the verification is based on actions involving an authorized entity (e.g. confirmation by an authorized user).

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the verification of software updates via a trust relationship concerning authenticity and …

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the verification of software updates via a trust relationship concerning authenticity and integrity a) and the performing entity b), and the functional assessment of the completeness of the IXIT documentation c).

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall apply the test units a-b as specified in the Test case 5.3-9-1.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each network based update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the verification of integrity and authenticity relies on a valid trust relationship according to "Description" and "Security Guarantees". A valid trust relationship includes:

- authenticated communication channels; or
- presence on a network that requires the device to possess a critical security parameter or password to join; or
- digital signature based verification of the update; or
- confirmation by the user; or
- a comparable secure functionality.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall functionally assess whether update mechanisms that are not documented in IXIT 7-UpdMech are available via a network interface on the DUT.

EXAMPLE: Network traffic analyser tools support the discovery of network-based update mechanisms.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- each update mechanism is effective for the verification of authenticity of software updates; and
- each update mechanism is effective for the verification of integrity of software updates; and
- the verification of authenticity and integrity of software updates is based on a valid trust relationship; and
- every discovered network-based update mechanism is documented in the IXIT.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation). Functional assessment: the TL tests the DUT itself.

parts.name: objective
parts.prose: The test group addresses the provision 5.3-11.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the method and content of information for the user about required security updates

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the method and content of information for the user about required security updates.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the method to inform the user about the availability of required security updates is recognizable and apparent according to "User Notification".

EXAMPLE 1: A notification via user interface, push message, e-mail is recognizable.

EXAMPLE 2: A sufficiently sized pop-up using short and concise language is apparent.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech, the TL shall assess whether the user notification on required security updates includes information about the risks mitigated by the update according to "User Notification".

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if for all update mechanisms which check for security updates:

- the method to inform the user about required security updates is recognizable and apparent; and
- the notification on required security updates includes information about the risks mitigated by the update.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-12.

NOTE: When the basic functioning of the DUT is never disrupted by a software update, no user notification is necessary.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of user notifications in case of disruptive software updates

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of user notifications in case of disruptive software updates.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For each update mechanism in IXIT 7-UpdMech the TL shall check whether the mechanism supports user notification in case of disruptive software updates according to "User Notification".

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if for each update mechanism:

- the user is appropriately notified by the DUT or another communication channel about the disruption of basic functioning during the software update.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

parts.name: objective
parts.prose:
The test group addresses the provision 5.3-13.

The defined support period describes the time span during which the manufacturer provides support regarding software updates. The defined software update support period is expected to be published even when no software updates are supported, in which case it indicates the absence of software updates.

controls.title: Conceptual assessment of the publication of the defined support period

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The purpose of this test case is the conceptual assessment of the publication of the defined support period.

parts.name: item
parts.prose:
The TL shall assess whether access to the "Publication of Support Period" in IXIT 2-UserInfo is understandable and comprehensible for a user with limited technical knowledge (see clause D.3).

EXAMPLE: With help of the model designation of the DUT the user finds the support period over a search engine on website of the manufacturer.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- the publication of software update support period is understandable and comprehensible for a user with limited technical knowledge.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Conceptual assessment: the TL examines the documentation of the supplier (ICS, IXIT, user documentation).

controls.title: Functional assessment of the publication of the defined support period

parts.name: statement

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall functionally check whether the user information on accessing the resource for publishing the defined support period according to "Publication of Support Period" in IXIT 2-UserInfo is provided as described.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall functionally check whether the resource for publishing the defined support period according to "Publication of Support Period" in IXIT 2-UserInfo is accessible without restrictions (like e.g. a registration prior to the access).

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The TL shall functionally check whether the published support period according to "Publication of Support Period" in IXIT 2-UserInfo actually defines the support period with respect to the updateable software components as described in "Support Period" in IXIT 2-UserInfo.

parts.name: assignment-of-verdict
parts.prose:
The verdict PASS is assigned if:

- the access to the resource for publishing the defined support period to the user is provided as described in the IXIT; and
- the access to the resource for publishing the defined support period is unrestricted; and
- the defined support period is published.

The verdict FAIL is assigned otherwise.
